agent: outliner wave, reader A (the window and its list)
question: What builds the outliner window, where it is shown and hidden, what the nine view switches and the configuration window do and where they are kept, what the list holds and in what order, when it is rebuilt, and what a click on it does.

structs.name: COutLiner
structs.comment: **The outliner**: the list down the right of the in-game screen. No RTTI of its own (the class name comes from CButtonObserverGlue<COutLiner>), no vftable. One per CTopBar, at CTopBar +0x378, made by `operator new(0x80)` and COutLiner::COutLiner in CTopBar::Build (0x6CC5C1..0x6CC5F9) and destroyed there before the next. Holds the `outliner` window, the `outliner_configuration` window, the bottom cap, the ten view switches by section kind and a vector of twelve COutlinerSection. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section A.
structs.evidence: Size from `push 0x80; call operator_new` at 0x6CC5C1 immediately before `call 0x6A3210` at 0x6CC5E3 with the new block in ECX; the store of the result at +0x378 at 0x6CC5F9. The class name is the template argument of RTTI `.?AV?$CButtonObserverGlue@VCOutLiner@@@@`, whose vftable 0x15D06F8 the constructor writes at this+0x1C. Wrong if some other path allocates the object with a different size - none found: COutLiner::COutLiner has one caller.

structs.name: COutlinerSection
structs.comment: One section of the outliner, an element of COutLiner's vector (+0x08). The name is ours. Twelve are made, kind 0 to 11: 1 land combat, 2 naval combat, 3 air combat, 4 land units, 5 naval units, 6 air units, 7 allied objectives, 8 our bombings, 9 hostile bombing; 11 holds the CTitleMember header rows; 0 and 10 are never filled. `shown` is whether the section was built at the last rebuild, `wanted` whether its switch is on now; COutLiner::Refresh copies wanted into shown at the end of every pass.
structs.evidence: Stride 0x18 in every index (`kind * 0x18 + sections_begin`, e.g. 0x6A7534..0x6A7543, and the vector growth 0x6A93D0 dividing by 0x18); the element copy 0x6A97B0 copies a dword, two bytes at +4/+5 and a CList at +8; the constructor 0x6A28C0 writes kind at +0, zeroes +4, +5 and the list (+8 head, +0xC tail, +0x10 count, +0x14 byte). The twelve: the loop `cmp [ebp-0x28], 0xC` at 0x6A3649 of COutLiner::COutLiner, constructing at 0x6A3656 and pushing at 0x6A3681. Wrong if the element is larger than 0x18 - the vector arithmetic would not divide by 0x18.

struct_fields.name: window
struct_fields.comment: The `outliner` window (interface/outliner.gui), made by the gui's window factory (slot 11) in COutLiner::COutLiner. Its +0x5B (the CGuiObject at +0x18, is_open +0x43) is what COutLiner::IsVisible answers.
struct_fields.evidence: `*param_1 = gui->slot11("outliner", ...)` at 0x6A3588..0x6A35A0; every element lookup (slot 0x48 checkbox, 0x7C list box) goes through it; IsVisible 0x6A7D6E reads [[this]+0x5B].

struct_fields.name: max_list_height
struct_fields.comment: The tallest the list may be: ((screen_height - 358) / 16) * 16 - 48, C division. 672 at 1080. Hardcoded.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x6A35D7..0x6A3602: graphics +0x6B9C0 (screen_height, confirmed live elsewhere) through 0xA75390, `sub 0x166`, the signed shift by 4 with the rounding bias, `shl 4`, `sub 0x30`, stored at this+4; compared with the summed row heights at the end of Refresh (0x6A7570 area) and FillList.

struct_fields.name: sections_begin
struct_fields.comment: Begin of the vector of twelve COutlinerSection, kind = index. +0x0C end, +0x10 capacity end, +0x14 the allocator.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructed empty by 0x6A8EA0(this+8) and filled by twelve push_backs (0x6A92D0) in the constructor; indexed `kind * 0x18 + [this+8]` throughout Refresh, Show, Hide, FillList and SetSectionWanted (0x6A8610).

struct_fields.name: sections_end
struct_fields.evidence: vector push_back 0x6A92F0 compares and advances [this+4] of the vector at COutLiner+8.

struct_fields.name: sections_capacity_end
struct_fields.comment: Capacity end of the section vector.

struct_fields.name: configuration_window
struct_fields.comment: The `outliner_configuration` window: a list of nine `outliner_configuration_entry` rows (CConfigMember, kinds 1..9) and a close button. Hidden at the end of the constructor and by its close button; **no code found shows it**.
struct_fields.evidence: gui slot 11 ("outliner_configuration") stored at this+0x18, 0x6A3695..0x6A36B0; its `close_button` gets the observer at +0x1C; slot 14 (Hide) on its +0x18 at 0x6A40B1 and in OnConfigurationClose 0x6A7D9C. fieldchain --holder 0x378 --field 0x18 finds no reader outside these (positive control: --field 0x7C on the same holder finds the one writer).

struct_fields.name: close_observer
struct_fields.comment: A CButtonObserverGlue<COutLiner> held by value (vftable 0x15D06F8, owner at +0x20, the click handler COutLiner::OnConfigurationClose at +0x24, the other seven handler slots null), attached to the configuration window's close_button.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x6A3210: [this+0x1C] = 0x15D06F8, [this+0x20] = this, [this+0x24] = 0x6A7D80, +0x28..+0x44 zeroed; the glue's slot 2 (0x6A89E0) calls [glue+8], which is this+0x24.

struct_fields.name: bottom_icon
struct_fields.comment: The `outliner_bottom` icon, made as a stand-alone element by the gui (slot 31) and attached to the window as `bottom`; Refresh and FillList move it to just under the list (x 0, y the list's y plus the list's height).
struct_fields.evidence: gui slot 0x7C("outliner_bottom") at 0x6A3743, stored at this+0x48; `bottom` at 0x6A3787, window slot 0x58("bottom", it); 0x6A75F8 and 0x6A7675 call 0xAA2290 on [this+0x48] with the point built from the list position slot 0x3C and the height.

struct_fields.name: view_switches
struct_fields.comment: The ten view switches by section kind: [1] outliner_view_landcombat, [2] _navalcombat, [3] _aircombat, [4] _landunits, [5] _navalunits, [6] _airunits, [7] _ao, [8] _bombonus, [9] _bombonthem; [0] is always null. Each is given the group name `outliner` (element slot 30), which is how CInGameIdler::GetElementTooltip routes its tooltip to COutLiner::BuildTooltip.
struct_fields.evidence: The nine stores after the nine name strings at 0x6A3A06..0x6A3C66 (landunits -> param_1[0x17] = +0x5C, airunits [0x19], navalunits [0x18], landcombat [0x14], aircombat [0x16], navalcombat [0x15], bombonus [0x1B], bombonthem [0x1C], ao [0x1A]); index = (offset - 0x4C) / 4 is the kind passed to SetSectionWanted in Refresh (0x6A42E5..0x6A44xx) and to GetOutlinerKindTitle in BuildTooltip (0x6A86A4..0x6A86CC). The loop over [this+0x4C+i*4] for i < 10 calling element slot 0x78 with "outliner".

struct_fields.name: force_rebuild
struct_fields.comment: Set by CSetCountryControllerCommand's Execute (0x6D42CD) when who controls a country changes; Refresh rebuilds the list when it is set and clears it.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0x6A330A writes 0. Refresh 0x6A4A85..0x6A4A97: `local_25 = this->+0x7C != 0; if so +0x7C = 0`, local_25 being the rebuild flag. Only writer of 1: 0x6D42CD, through [[x+0x378]+0x7C] (fieldchain).

struct_fields.name: kind
struct_fields.comment: The section's kind, 0..11, the same number its rows answer from slot 12 (GetKind).
struct_fields.evidence: Written by the constructor 0x6A28C0 from its argument; read by COutlinerSection::GetKind 0x6A2B30 and compared with a title row's kind in FillList (0x6A7F9B).

struct_fields.name: shown
struct_fields.comment: Whether the section was built into the list at the last rebuild (set from `wanted` at the end of every Refresh).
struct_fields.evidence: IsShown 0x6A29F0 reads +4; SetShownAndWanted 0x6A29D0 writes +4 and +5; Refresh's last loop (0x6A752B..) calls it with IsWanted for kinds 0..9.

struct_fields.name: wanted
struct_fields.comment: Whether the section's switch is on. Mirrored in the settings' `outliner` list by SetWanted.
struct_fields.evidence: SetWanted 0x6A2A10 writes +5 and adds or removes the kind in GameSettings +0x164; IsWanted 0x6A2B10 reads +5 and gates the building of the section in Refresh.

struct_fields.name: members
struct_fields.comment: The section's rows, in list order. Owned: ClearMembers deletes each (slot 0, flag 1) and frees the nodes. The title section (kind 11) is never cleared.
struct_fields.evidence: AddMember 0x6A2920 appends at +8 (head +8, tail +0xC, count +0x10); GetMembers 0x6A2B40 returns this+8; ClearMembers 0x6A2B60 walks it calling [[node]]+0 with 1 and frees the list through 0x6A9270. Hide (0x6A7C80) and Refresh clear kinds 0..9 only.

struct_fields.name: outliner
struct_fields.comment: The outliner. Freed (COutLiner::~COutLiner, free) and made again (operator new 0x80, COutLiner::COutLiner) by every CTopBar::Build; read by CTopBar::SyncOutliner, CTopBar::OnOutlinerButton, CTopBar_OutlinerTooltip, the custom-game bar (0x426D61) and CSetCountryControllerCommand's Execute (0x6D42C7). Was `outliner_state`, void*, 'unidentified'.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x6CC59F..0x6CC5F9 in CTopBar::Build; the constructor at 0x6A3210 builds the `outliner` window. Was recorded as an unidentified 0x80-byte object; the type is what changed.

struct_fields.name: outliner_auto_hidden
struct_fields.comment: Set by CTopBar::SyncOutliner when it closes an open outliner because a country view or the ledger opened, and cleared when it reopens it once both are gone. Was `outliner_flag`, uint8_t, 'unidentified'.
struct_fields.evidence: SyncOutliner 0x6CBA3A..0x6CBA51: IsVisible true -> OnOutlinerButton (which hides) -> byte = 1; 0x6CBB01..0x6CBB3A: byte set, IsVisible false, no view open and idler +0x1CE0 null -> OnOutlinerButton (which shows) -> byte = 0. Only those two writers besides the CTopBar constructor's zero. Name and type change, the offset does not.

struct_fields.name: outliner_sections
struct_fields.comment: The settings file's `outliner = { ... }` list: the kinds 1..9 whose switch is on, and **10 while the outliner is open**. Order means nothing. Replaced whole when the key is read (CList_FreeAndClear then the int list, CSettings::LoadKey 0x4602E8); with no key the settings constructor gives {10, 4, 5, 6} - open, land, naval and air units. The install's settings.txt ships {1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9}. Written in memory by COutlinerSection::SetWanted, COutLiner::Show/Hide and CConfigMember; read by COutLiner::COutLiner.
struct_fields.evidence: GetGameSettings + 0x4600B0 (`add eax, 0x164`) at every use; the constructor 0x45FA80 zeroes +0x164..+0x16C and the byte +0x170, then appends 0xA, 4, 5, 6 (0x45FBF7, 0x45FC42, 0x45FC8D, 0x45FCD8); FINDINGS-definitions.md's CSettings table has `outliner` (token 0x1D8) landing at +0x164. Wrong if the loader appended instead of replacing - it calls CList_FreeAndClear (0x50D1E0) on +0x164 first, at 0x4602EE.

addresses.name: COutLiner::COutLiner
addresses.comment: **Builds the outliner.** 0x6A3210..0x6A40E4, bare `ret`, one caller (CTopBar::Build, 0x6CC5E3). Makes the `outliner` window (+0x00); max_list_height (+0x04) = ((screen_height - 358) / 16) * 16 - 48; twelve COutlinerSection, kinds 0..11 (+0x08); the `outliner_configuration` window (+0x18) with the close button wired to COutLiner::OnConfigurationClose (+0x1C); the `outliner_bottom` icon attached as `bottom` (+0x48). From the settings' `outliner` list (GameSettings +0x164): every kind in it but 10 is SetShownAndWanted(1); 10 means 'open'. The configuration list gets a CConfigMember for each kind 1..9, checked when the kind is in the settings. The nine view switches are found by name into +0x4C[kind], each given the group name `outliner`, and each checked (CCheckBox_Check) when its kind is in the settings, else unchecked - in the order 4, 6, 5, 1, 3, 2, 8, 9, 7. The configuration window is hidden. Last, **when 10 was in the settings, COutLiner::Show** - so the outliner opens with the game when it was open when the settings were written. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Read whole in Ghidra's decompilation of a copy of the project and on the listing: the string pushes at 0x6A3588 (outliner), 0x6A3695 (outliner_configuration), 0x6A3A06..0x6A3C66 (the nine switches); the settings walks through 0x4600B0; the call 0x6A40C4 -> 0x6A7800 under the byte set when a value is 10. Bare `ret` at 0x6A40E4; this in ECX (`mov [ebp-0x5bc], ecx`). Wrong if a settings value other than 10 opened the window - only `cmp [..], 0xA` sets that byte.

addresses.name: COutLiner::~COutLiner
addresses.comment: Destroys the close button's observer glue (+0x1C, vftable rewritten then 0x7E3880) and the section vector (0x6A8EE0 on +0x08). **It destroys neither window nor any row**: the members are freed only as list nodes. One caller, CTopBar::Build (0x6CC5AF), before it frees the block and makes a new outliner. Ghidra had named it a CButtonObserverGlue constructor.
addresses.evidence: 0x6A4130..0x6A4161, bare `ret`; writes 0x15D06F8 at this+0x1C and calls 0x7E3880 on it, then 0x6A8EE0(this+8), whose per-element 0x6A9750 frees the element's node list through 0x6A9270. Caller 0x6CC5AF with ECX = [esi+0x378], followed by free.

addresses.name: COutLiner::Refresh
addresses.comment: **The outliner's pass, every frame while it is open** (CTopBar::SyncOutliner, once a frame from CInGameIdler::Update through 0x64F850 and CTopBar::Update). 0x6A4280..0x6A76C4, bare `ret`. Nothing when the window is not visible (+0x5B). (1) Each view switch: checked -> SetSectionWanted(kind, 1); unchecked and the section shown -> SetSectionWanted(kind, 0); kinds 4, 6, 5, 1, 3, 2, 8, 9, 7. (2) Builds the wanted contents (OutlinerScan_Init): every unit of the player's country (CCountry::GetUnits) that is top-level for the outliner (no parent, or a fleet or air unit whose parent is a land unit - 0x5D39F0): an air unit, unless any unit above it has an AI agent (+0x198) or it is all carrier air groups with a base whose slot 1 is true (a carrier), goes to the air list; a fleet, unless any unit above it has an AI agent, to the naval list; a land unit with no parent to the land list - each through Outliner_AddUnitTree, which adds the unit and, where its +0xB4 byte is set, its children below it, recursively. Then OutlinerScan_CollectCombats. (3) Rebuild when +0x7C is set (cleared), or for any kind 1..9 when a section not shown has rows, or a shown one's row count or any row's object differs from the new list in order (units by the row's unit, battles by CAirCombatMember_GetCombatIfCurrent, bombings by CBombCombatMember::GetCombatIfCurrent; allied objectives by count only, the two lists' sizes summed). (4) No rebuild: slot 8 (Update) of every row of every shown section. Rebuild: the list's scroll position saved, the list emptied, kinds 0..9 cleared, and for kinds 1..9 in order whose section is wanted, a row object per entry (CCombatMember, CNavalCombatMember, CAirCombatMember, CArmyMember, CNavyMember with the base's province or else the unit's own, CAirMember the same, CAlliedObjectiveMember for each record of game state +0xB9C[player] with 1 then of +0xBAC[player] with 0, CBombCombatMember for 8 and 9), kept in the section and added under its title by COutLiner::AddSectionRows; the scroll position restored. Every pass ends with each section's shown set to its wanted, the list's height set to min(the rows' summed height, max_list_height) and the bottom cap put under it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, decompilation and listing (scratchpad readerA/refresh.txt). The loop over the units 0x6A47A7..0x6A4A4C (0x5D39F0, IsAir slot 0x44, the +0x1E0 / +0x198 walk, CUnit_AllSubUnitsAreCag, base +0x98 slot 1, IsNaval 0x40, 0x5B9B40 + IsLand 0x3C); the nine comparisons 0x6A4AC8..0x6A5779; the rebuild from the scroll position saved (0x62D8B0 at 0x6A5CE0) and the clears (0x6A5D92) through nine calls of 0x6A8170 to ListBox_RestoreScroll at 0x6A750B; the tail 0x6A759D..0x6A76A1. Wrong if the call at 0x655AEF were conditional on something other than the game-mode byte at 0x64F88B - cfg.py shows 0x655AE7 reached from both arms of the orders-view test above it.

addresses.name: COutLiner::Show
addresses.comment: **Opens the outliner.** 0x6A7800..0x6A7C7B, bare `ret`. Shows the window (its +0x18 slot 13); adds 10 to the settings' `outliner` list if absent; **makes ten new CTitleMember, kinds 0..9, appended to section 11 - every time, never freed**; then the battles straight into sections 1, 2 and 3 (Outliner_CollectCombatsOfKind with kinds 1, 2, 3 on one list that is not emptied between calls, so section 2 also gets the land battles and section 3 the land and naval ones, each as a row of the section's own class - corrected by the next Refresh), and COutLiner::FillList. Two callers: COutLiner::COutLiner (0x6A40C4) and CTopBar::OnOutlinerButton (0x6CFFA3). **The ten titles a Show leaves behind are the 30-widget leak** measured in FINDINGS-guilive.md: Hide never clears section 11, so each close and open - which every full-screen view causes through CTopBar::SyncOutliner - keeps ten outliner_header_entry windows (outliner_header, entry_text) alive.
addresses.evidence: Listing: the CList_Contains / append of 0xA on GameSettings +0x164; the loop `for i < 10` with operator new(0x2C), CTitleMember::CTitleMember(i) and AddMember on [this+8]+0x108 (kind 11); the three calls of 0x6A1850 at 0x6A7A47, 0x6A7AF9, 0x6A7BAB on [ebp-0x1C] with no CList_FreeAndClear between them (that comes once, after FillList). Hide (0x6A7C80) clears kinds 0..9 only. The leak's widget count (10 x 3) and names match the live measurement in FINDINGS-guilive.md. Wrong if CTitleMember::CTitleMember did not build an outliner_header_entry - reader C's fragment has it building one.

addresses.name: COutLiner::Hide
addresses.comment: **Closes the outliner.** Takes 10 out of the settings' `outliner` list, hides the window (its +0x18 slot 14), empties the list box and clears the rows of kinds 0..9 (not 11, the titles). One caller, CTopBar::OnOutlinerButton (0x6CFED4).
addresses.evidence: 0x6A7C80..0x6A7D50, bare `ret`: CList_RemoveValue(10) on GameSettings +0x164, window slot 0x38, list box (`outliner_list`, window slot 0x7C) slot 0x24, then COutlinerSection::ClearMembers for i < 10.

addresses.name: COutLiner::IsVisible
addresses.comment: Whether the outliner window is on screen: the window's +0x5B (its CGuiObject at +0x18, is_open at +0x43). Six callers: CTopBar::SyncOutliner (three), CTopBar::Build (0x6CC5FF, to pick the button's frame), CTopBar::OnOutlinerButton, and the custom-game bar 0x426D40.
addresses.evidence: 0x6A7D60..0x6A7D7A: `mov ecx,[this]; mov dl,[ecx+0x5B]`; findRefs --callers gives the six.

addresses.name: COutLiner::OnConfigurationClose
addresses.comment: The configuration window's close_button: hides the configuration window and calls 0xAB1CE0 with the settings object in ESI (inferred to apply and write the settings; not read). Reached only through the glue at +0x1C.
addresses.evidence: 0x6A7D80..0x6A7DB1: [this+0x18]+0x18 slot 14, then GetGameSettings, `mov esi, eax`, call 0xAB1CE0. No direct callers; the constructor stores 0x6A7D80 at this+0x24, the glue's first handler. That 0xAB1CE0 writes the file is inferred from its being called after GetGameSettings at all five sites and after the settings singleton is replaced at 0x6F7605.

addresses.name: COutLiner::FillList
addresses.comment: Lays the rows already in the sections into the list: notes the list's height, empties it, and for kinds 0..11 except 11 whose section is shown and has rows, adds the section's title (the first CTitleMember of section 11 whose kind matches) and then its rows; sets the list's height to min(height, max_list_height), puts the bottom cap under it and calls the list's slot 27. One caller, COutLiner::Show. Its starting height is the list's before the emptying, so it is only right because Hide emptied the list first.
addresses.evidence: 0x6A7DC0..0x6A816C, bare `ret`; the loop `if (0xB < i)` exit, IsShown, `GetKind != 0xB`, CTitleMember_GetKindField compared with the section's kind, list slot 4 (add) for title and rows, list slot 0x6C at the end.

addresses.name: COutLiner::AddSectionRows
addresses.signature: int __thiscall COutLiner::AddSectionRows(COutLiner* this, int kind, CList<COutLinerMember*>* rows)
addresses.comment: Adds one section to the list and returns the height it added. **Nothing at all for a section with no rows - not even its title.** Otherwise the section's title (the first CTitleMember of section 11 with that kind) and then the rows, appended; when the list already holds rows, COutLiner::FindSectionEnd is asked where the kind's run ends and the rows are inserted before that row (the title only when none is listed yet), else appended. Heights are each row's own (its +0x1C table's slot 5), without the list's spacing. Nine callers, all in COutLiner::Refresh.
addresses.evidence: 0x6A8170..0x6A84C6, `ret 8`; `if (rows->count != 0)` at the top; the title search through 0x6AE710; list slots 4 and 6; findRefs --callers gives the nine in 0x6A5FCD..0x6A7492.

addresses.name: COutLiner::FindSectionEnd
addresses.signature: void** __thiscall COutLiner::FindSectionEnd(COutLiner* this, void** out, int kind, bool* titleListed) @EAX
addresses.comment: Walks the list's rows: sets *titleListed where a title row (slot 12 = 11) of `kind` is listed, and answers the first row after the run of rows whose slot 12 is `kind`, or null. One caller, COutLiner::AddSectionRows.
addresses.evidence: 0x6A84D0..0x6A8607, `ret 0xC`; row slot 0x30 (12) compared with 0xB and with the kind; the out pointer written at the end.

addresses.name: COutLiner::SetSectionWanted
addresses.signature: void __thiscall COutLiner::SetSectionWanted(COutLiner* this, int kind, bool wanted)
addresses.comment: COutlinerSection::SetWanted on section `kind`. Called by Refresh for each view switch every frame, and by CConfigMember::OnChecked / OnUnchecked.
addresses.evidence: 0x6A8610..0x6A8630, `ret 8`: `kind * 0x18 + [this+8]`, call 0x6A2A10. Twenty callers (findRefs).

addresses.name: COutLiner::BuildTooltip
addresses.signature: GuiTooltipText* __thiscall COutLiner::BuildTooltip(COutLiner* this, GuiTooltipText* out, CGuiObject* element) @EAX
addresses.comment: **The tooltip of anything in the outliner.** A view switch: the section's title (GetOutlinerKindTitle(kind) - 'Land Combat', 'Our Bombings'...). Otherwise each row of the list in turn is asked its slot 14 (OwnsElement) and, where it says yes, its slot 13 (BuildTooltip) - the last row to say yes wins. One caller, CTopBar_OutlinerTooltip, from CInGameIdler::GetElementTooltip for an element whose group is `outliner`.
addresses.evidence: 0x6A8640..0x6A88B5, `ret 8`; the loop over [this+0x4C+i*4] for i < 10 at 0x6A8691..0x6A8739 pushing i and out to 0x6AE0D0 (`add esp, 8` - two cdecl arguments); the walk of the list's rows calling [vft+0x38](element) and [vft+0x34](tmp, element).

addresses.name: ListBox_GetContentSize
addresses.comment: The size of a list box's rows as a pair of shorts: (0, 0) with no rows (+0x5C); for a vertical list (+0xF4 set) the first row's width and the sum over the rows of the spacing (+0xE0) and each row's height; otherwise the summed widths and the first row's height. The outliner's copy; rows are walked from +0x54.
addresses.evidence: 0x6A90A0..0x6A925F, `ret 4`; reads listbox +0x5C, +0x54, +0xF4, +0xE0 and each row's slot 5 through its node; out built by 0x414860. Called from Refresh (0x6A474B, 0x6A759D, 0x6A7614) and FillList.

addresses.name: Outliner_AddUnitTree
addresses.comment: Appends `unit`, then - only where it has children (CUnit +0x1E4) and its byte +0xB4 is set (the outliner's expanded flag, read here and not written) - each child in the children list's order, recursively. So the tree is flattened depth first, a unit's subordinates straight after it, and a collapsed unit hides everything below it. Four callers: itself and Refresh's three unit lists.
addresses.evidence: 0x6A4170..0x6A4273, bare `ret`, callers `add esp, 8`; CUnit::GetChildren (0x5B9B70) count test, 0x60F9A0 (`mov al, [eax+0xB4]`) with EAX = the unit, the recursive call at 0x6A4266.

addresses.name: OutlinerScan_Init
addresses.comment: Initialises the stack block Refresh gathers the wanted contents in (0x158 bytes or more): +0 the player's controlled provinces (kept, not used), then empty lists every 0x10 bytes from +0x04, vectors at +0x114 and +0x134, lists at +0x144 and +0x154. What the outliner fills: +0x04 land battles, +0x24 naval, +0x44 air, +0x64 hostile bombings, +0x84 our bombings, +0xA4 land units, +0xC4 naval units, +0xE4 air units. One caller, Refresh (0x6A4777).
addresses.evidence: 0x6A16E0..0x6A184B, `ret 4`, this in ECX (`mov [ebp-0x24], ecx`); seventeen 0x432630 list inits and the destructor OutlinerScan_Destroy's matching frees. The use of each list: Refresh passes +0xA4/+0xC4/+0xE4 to Outliner_AddUnitTree (lea [ebp-0xF8/-0xD8/-0xB8] with the block at [ebp-0x19C]) and OutlinerScan_CollectCombats writes the others.

addresses.name: OutlinerScan_Destroy
addresses.comment: Frees what OutlinerScan_Init made: CList::FreeNodes on +0x154 and +0x144, the vectors of lists at +0x134 and +0x114, and CList_FreeAndClear on the seventeen lists from +0x124 down to +0x04. One caller, the end of Refresh.
addresses.evidence: 0x6A76D0..0x6A77F8, bare `ret`; called at 0x6A76B0 with ECX = the block.

addresses.name: OutlinerScan_CollectCombats
addresses.comment: **Which battles the outliner lists**: for every unit of `country` (CCountry::GetUnits, in its order) that is in a battle (+0x11C > 0) or a bombing (+0x110): each battle on its list (+0x114) that is live (slot 9) goes, once, to land (kind 1, +0x04), naval (2, +0x24) or air (3, +0x44); its bombing goes, once, to **our bombings (+0x84) where the unit is an air unit (IsAir) and its owner (+0x124) is the player**, else to hostile bombing (+0x64) - with no test of the bombing's kind or which side the unit is on. A branch for kinds 4 and 5 off the battle list tests `4 || 5 || 5` (kind 6 never) and is dead, bombings never being on that list. One caller, Refresh (0x6A4A73).
addresses.evidence: 0x6A1F50..0x6A28B0, bare `ret`, caller `add esp, 8`; 0x5BFF50 (+0x11C > 0), 0x5BFF60 (+0x110 != 0), 0x5BFE70 (+0x114), combat slots 0x2C (kind) and 0x24 (live), CList find 0x44E7F0 before each append; the compares at 0x6A241E, 0x6A2424, 0x6A242A are 4, 5, 5. That bombings live only at +0x110 is the record's CUnit join routine ('a bombing is stored at CUnit +0x110, anything else appended to +0x114').

addresses.name: Outliner_CollectCombatsOfKind
addresses.signature: void __cdecl Outliner_CollectCombatsOfKind(CList<CCombat*>* out, CCountry* country, int kind, bool anyOwner)
addresses.comment: The one-kind form of OutlinerScan_CollectCombats, appending to `out` the live battles (and bombings, by +0x110) of kind `kind` that `country`'s units are in, each once and not already in `out`; for kinds 4 to 6 only where the unit's owner is the player and it is an air unit, unless `anyOwner`. Three callers, all in COutLiner::Show, with kinds 1, 2 and 3 and anyOwner 0.
addresses.evidence: 0x6A1850..0x6A1F48, bare `ret`; callers push (0, kind, country, &list) and `add esp, 0x10` (0x6A7A3B..0x6A7A4C).

addresses.name: CTopBar::SyncOutliner
addresses.comment: **The outliner's frame.** Called at the end of CTopBar::Update (once a frame, through 0x64F850 from CInGameIdler::Update) and of CTopBar::Show, and by the custom-game bar (0x4273A4). With an outliner (+0x378): when it is open, **COutLiner::Refresh**. Then, when the idler's open country view (views[open_view], its IsOpen) is open or the ledger (+0x1CE0) is: an open outliner is closed through CTopBar::OnOutlinerButton and outliner_auto_hidden (+0x37C) set, and `topbar_outlinerbutton` hidden; otherwise the button shown again where it is hidden and the top bar is. Last, with outliner_auto_hidden set, the outliner closed and neither view nor ledger open, OnOutlinerButton reopens it and the byte is cleared. So the outliner goes away behind every full-screen screen and comes back after it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section A. **Revised 2026-11-03**: the callees are read; it was 'likely' and a guess.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole on a copy of the project: 0x6CB94C IsVisible -> 0x6CB95B Refresh; the view and +0x1CE0 tests; 0x6CBA45 / 0x6CBB3A OnOutlinerButton with the +0x37C writes; the button's +0x43 (is_open) read and its slots 13 / 14. CTopBar::Update calls it at 0x6CB5EF; CInGameIdler::Update calls 0x64F850 at 0x655AEF on its main path (cfg.py: 0x655AE7 is reached from both arms above it). What changed: comment and confidence; name and signature kept.

Two callers, CCgmBar slot 4 (0x424961) and 0x42789C. The class is inferred from its callers.

Wrong if idler slot 65 were not the top bar - it is read +0x378 of, which only CTopBar's outliner field answers among the readers found.
